brand.name: The Marti School
brand.tagline: Turkish language, culture and friendship, every Saturday.

home.heroSubtitle: A weekend school in Columbia, Maryland where children learn Turkish, celebrate their culture, and make friends who share their story.
home.whySubtitle: More than a language class. A place where children grow up proud of where they come from.
home.why1Title: Teachers who speak it at home
home.why1Body: Every teacher is a fluent Turkish speaker trained to teach heritage learners, whether your child is starting from zero or already chatting with grandparents.
home.why2Title: The right class, not just the right age
home.why2Body: Children are placed by ability, so nobody is bored and nobody is lost. We review placement every term.
home.why3Title: Culture you can hear and dance
home.why3Body: Folk dance, music, holidays and stories sit right alongside reading and writing, because a language lives inside a culture.
home.why4Body: Attendance and detailed termly reports are online any time, so you know how your child is really doing.
home.why5Body: Saturdays only. Serious learning that still leaves the rest of family life alone.
home.why6Body: Families across Maryland who share a language and a heritage, meeting every week and celebrating together.
home.programsSubtitle: From first words to full conversations.
home.howSubtitle: From application to your first Saturday.
home.how1Body: Tell us about your child. It takes about five minutes.
home.how2Body: Our principal reads every application, usually within two or three days.
home.how3Body: Once approved, your child gets a MARTI student ID and a login for the family portal.
home.how4Body: Meet the teacher, meet the class, and get started.
home.ctaTitle: Give your child their language back

about.title: About the school
about.subtitle: A Saturday school run by Turkish-American families, for Turkish-American children.
about.storyP1: The Marti School is the weekend school of the Maryland Turkish-American Inhabitants, which has been bringing families together since 2003.
about.storyP2: It started the way good schools usually do, with parents worrying about something. Their children were growing up in Maryland speaking perfect English and slowly losing the Turkish their grandparents spoke.
about.storyP3: Today we teach Turkish language, culture, history and folk arts in classes grouped by ability. Still every Saturday, still run by families who refuse to let a heritage quietly disappear.
about.missionBody: To give Turkish-American children real fluency in their heritage language and a confident, lived connection to their culture.
about.value1Body: Turkish is not an after-school hobby. It is a family inheritance, and we teach it that seriously.
about.value2Body: Fluent at home or starting from nothing, placement by ability means every child has a class where they fit.
about.value3Body: Children learn a culture by living it: dancing it, cooking it, celebrating it, arguing about it.
about.value4Body: This school is run by families. Parents see real progress data and have a real say.
about.joinBody: Whether you want to enroll a child or teach with us, we would love to hear from you.

programs.title: Our classes
programs.subtitle: Grouped by ability, taught every Saturday morning.
programs.scheduleSubtitle: Here is how the morning goes.
programs.ctaBody: Apply anyway. Our principal will place your child at the right level after a short chat.
programs.p1Desc: First words, songs and stories. Play-based Turkish for the youngest, with no reading or writing pressure.
programs.p2Desc: The Turkish alphabet, reading, and everyday conversation, mixed with games and cultural activities.
programs.p3Desc: Grammar, writing and comprehension, with Turkish history and geography woven through.
programs.p4Desc: Confident conversation, literature and essay writing. Prepares students for Turkish proficiency exams.
programs.p5Desc: For children who already speak Turkish at home but need reading, writing and formal grammar.
programs.p6Desc: Folk dance, music, crafts and holiday celebrations. Open to every enrolled student.

tuition.title: Tuition
tuition.subtitle: Clear pricing, with sibling discounts and financial help available.
tuition.placeholderNotice: These figures are examples. Please confirm current rates with the school office.
tuition.planStandardDesc: One Saturday class a week, with all materials included.
tuition.planFullDesc: Language class plus culture and folk arts. The complete Saturday.
tuition.planFamilyDesc: Two or more siblings, each on the full program.
tuition.faq1A: Yes. The second child pays a reduced rate and each additional sibling pays less again. The Family plan includes this automatically.
tuition.faq2Q: What if we cannot afford it?
tuition.faq2A: No family is turned away for money reasons. Contact the school office in confidence and we will work something out.
tuition.faq3A: Tuition is billed monthly across the school year. Families who prefer to pay for the year up front get a discount.
tuition.faq4Q: Can we join partway through the year?
tuition.faq4A: Yes. Tuition is prorated from the month your child starts, and placement is by ability, so joining later is no problem.
tuition.faq5A: Optional trips and the end-of-year festival costume fee are billed separately, and always announced in advance.
tuition.faq6Q: Can we try a class first?
tuition.faq6A: Of course. You are welcome to sit in on one Saturday before deciding. Just mention it on the registration form.
tuition.ctaBody: Registration takes about five minutes, and nothing is due until your child has a place.
